title: TAO moorings confirm record 2026 equatorial Pacific upper-ocean heat and a Nino3.4 SST peak above 1997-98 but level with 2015-16 (to October 2026); DOISST v2.1 adds 0.2 C to the 1997-98 margin
abstract: Question: by October 2026 the CPC OISST Nino3.4 index (+3.25 C) and the CPC GODAS 0-300 m heat content index (+3.39 C) showed a record El Nino, but the ERSSTv6 ONI and RONI did not. Do independent in situ data confirm the record, and how much of each margin comes from product artifacts and index definition? Approach: we used TAO/TRITON moorings as the arbiter. We compared DOISST v2.1, OI SST v2, ERSSTv5, COBE-SST2 and HadISST1 with the moorings at the same station-months, with matched 1991-2020 climatologies, matched station sets per event pair and station bootstrap intervals. For the subsurface we used TAO 0-300 m heat content, RG Argo and GODAS sampled at the moorings. Results: at matched moorings, the October 2026 Nino3.4 anomaly is 0.54 C above the largest 1997-98 month (95% interval 0.34 to 0.76) and 0.39 C above 2015-16 (-0.17 to 0.99). For 3-month peaks, 2026 is 0.30 C above 1997-98 (0.13 to 0.42) and level with 2015-16 (-0.02). DOISST v2.1 reads the 1997 peak 0.28 C too cold at the moorings and thus adds 0.21 C (0.13 to 0.30) to the 3-month margin over 1997-98; its error at warm anomalies falls from -0.24 C (1991-2004) to -0.08 C (2016-2026). COBE-SST2 and HadISST1 damp recent peaks more, and COBE-SST2 removes 0.28-0.34 C from the 2026 margins. The tropics (20S-20N) warmed by 0.36 C between the peaks, so relative indices do not show a clear record. The 0-300 m record is real: at matched moorings in 180-100W, 2026 is 0.92 C above 1997-98 (0.40 to 1.44) and 0.73 C above 2015-16; RG Argo and GODAS agree with TAO within the intervals. Limitations: the event was still growing; moorings are an input to the products; station sets are small; there are no mooring data for 1982-83; the cause of the DOISST 1997 error was not tested. Code, aggregate results and retrieval scripts are included.
